name: Kuwait Water Towers
features: Groups of 'mushroom' towers: a slim concrete stem under a broad conical tank, repeated across the city.
note: Wikipedia: built 1970-76 by VBB (chief architect Sune Lindström), five groups, 31 towers, reinforced concrete. Only one clear free photo of the towers themselves (2046x1400). File:Sunset at City.jpg (1290x919, CC BY-SA 4.0) is in the category but not checked.

name: Šerefudin's White Mosque
features: All-white mosque whose roof is a freely deformed quarter-dome pierced by five skylights; tubular minaret.
note: Both photos are tight, upward exterior views of the skylights and minaret (portrait). The only full exterior file is 783x653, under 800px. Interior photos also exist (File:Mosque skylights, Šerefudin's White Mosque.jpg, CC BY 2.0).

name: Universiti Teknologi Petronas
features: Five crescent-shaped buildings around a landscaped centre, linked by vast curved canopies that shade the walkways.
note: Wikipedia: first phase 2004, plan a five-pointed star of five semicircles. Pocket C shows the canopy over a teaching block. Other campus files in the category (Village Centre 3, Chancellor Complex subcategory) not checked.

name: Hassan II Bridge
features: Three parallel decks, two for road and one for tram, each carried on low concrete arches across the Bou Regreg.

photos.file: File:Bridge Pont hassan II, Oued Bou Regreg (25314990776).jpg

note: Completion given as 2010 (AKDN) or 2011 (Mimram). Many more photos in the category.

name: Islamic Cemetery Altach
features: Staggered rose-tinted concrete walls enclose five grave fields; prayer room behind an oak lattice of Islamic geometry.

photos.file: File:Islamic Cemetery of Altach Aerial view.JPG

note: Prayer space with Azra Akšamija. The category has 11 large CC BY-SA 3.0 AT photos (Muslimischer Friedhof, Robert-Koch-Straße 18 a, Altach 01-11) not all checked; 01 is the lattice seen from inside.

name: Madinat al-Zahra Museum
features: Museum set low into the ground like an excavation: a sequence of courtyards walled in pale concrete.
note: 39283697065 is a close view of the perforated wall; 40182199271 shows walls and courtyard. Award listing: Research Centre and Museum, Madinat al-Zahra.

name: The Datai Langkawi
features: Rainforest resort of timber-balconied blocks and villas set among the trees above Datai Bay.
note: Opened 1993; the main buildings sit about 40 m above and 300 m back from the sea, in the rainforest. Files DL2A---The-Dataï-Langkawi (1100px) are from the 2017-19 renovation by DL2A, so the panoramio photo is the better record of Kerry Hill's building. No Commons category found.

name: Kaédi Regional Hospital
features: Hospital of hand-fired local brick built as a sequence of domes and vaults, cooled and lit without machines.
note: Wikipedia is inconsistent on the date (infobox 1992, category 1989). File:KaediRegionalHospital1.JPG (4368x2912) is an interior corridor. Commons has two categories (Kaedi / Kaédi Regional Hospital).

name: Majara Residence
features: About 200 superadobe domes in bright colours, clustered like a village by the sea, with paths between them.

photos.file: File:Tahmineh Monzavi Photo Majara Residence Hormuz Iran View from the sea 2020.jpg

note: Iran has no freedom of panorama for recent buildings, so these uploads (apparently from the architects) may be challenged later. No Commons category found; File:Majara Residence.jpg (3823x2548) is a view from the top of a dome.

name: Banyuwangi International Airport
features: Low, naturally ventilated terminal under grass-covered roofs, its form drawn from the Osing people's headband.
note: Aga Khan record: completed 2018 (listed as Blimbingsari Airport). Reclaimed ship timber is mentioned in a travel guide only.

name: Argo Contemporary Art Museum
features: Old brick brewery turned art museum; a new frame carries floors and pitched roofs that float above the walls.
note: Argo Factory2 is an upward exterior view of the brick blocks and new roofs; Argo Factory 6 is the courtyard. File:Argo Factory Before Reconstruction.jpg (CC BY-SA 4.0) shows the brewery before conversion. Iran has no freedom of panorama, so uploads may be challenged.

name: Central Market, Koudougou
features: Market built of compressed earth blocks: rows of arched and vaulted stalls around shaded lanes.
note: Architect and earth-block construction from memory of the Aga Khan citation (Laurent Séchaud with Pierre Jequier); the akdn.org page was unreachable. Commons description says built 2005. Marché central is an overview from above; Grand marché is inside the vaulted lanes.

name: Jahad Metro Plaza
features: Metro entrance rebuilt as linked brick arches and vaults, about 300,000 handmade bricks, around a pedestrian plaza.
note: Only one good exterior file (6340x3870). Iran has no freedom of panorama, so it may be challenged. Mohammad Khavarian is named alongside the studio.

name: Entrepreneurship Development Institute of India
features: Brick campus of seven or eight blocks along two axes around courtyards, with deep arcades for the heat.
note: Aga Khan record: completed 1987, Ahmedabad (the campus is at Bhat, on the Gandhinagar side); databases say 1986. The 'Public domain' licence on EDII03 should be double-checked on its file page.

name: Yaama Mosque
features: Mud-brick hall with a central dome and four tapering corner towers, banded and crowned, built by its own village.
view: front elevation: the low prayer hall with its half-circle crenellations, the central dome behind, and the two front corner towers
note: No photo on Commons (also searched as 'Yamma'). Sources give: rectangular hypostyle hall begun 1962, central dome and four corner towers added later, towers with banded tapering walls more elaborate toward the pinnacle, parapet of half-circle crenellations. No dimensions are published, so tower and dome heights are proportioned from memory of published photos and may be off; the towers' top ornament is simplified to a ring of small crenellations and a rounded cone.

name: Royal Netherlands Embassy, Addis Ababa
features: A 140 m bar of red-ochre concrete laid level across a sloping eucalyptus grove, with a shallow pond on the roof.
view: long side elevation: the level two-storey bar over the falling ground, with the floor line and the roof pond's edge
note: No photo on Commons. Sources give 140 x 15 m, two floors both reachable from the ground thanks to the slope, red-tinted concrete walls, floors and ceilings, a roof designed as a shallow pond, and a driveway passing through the building at first-floor level. The driveway's position and the window pattern are not published in what I could read, so they are left out; the drawing is deliberately minimal. Architects worked as de Architectengroep (some sources credit Mecanoo for Van Gameren).

name: Mbaru Niang, Wae Rebo
by: Yori Antar with the Wae Rebo community
features: Tall conical houses of timber and thatch, rebuilt by the villagers with their ancestral techniques.

photos.file: File:WAE - Central area of Wae Rebo village, Flores, Indonesia, 2019.jpg

note: Shortlisted as 'Reconstruction of Mbaru Niang'. Architect credit (Yori Antar, Rumah Asuh) and 2011 completion are from memory; check. It is a vernacular reconstruction, so 'Historic precedent' fits best in the vocabulary.

name: Royal Academy for Nature Conservation
features: Stone building set into the forested hillside of the Ajloun reserve, entered across a bridge.

photos.file: File:Royal Academy for natural Reservation at Ajloun.jpg

note: Only one free photo (4032x3024), a night view of the stone wall and entrance bridge. Year 2014 from memory; check.

name: Intercontinental Hotel and Conference Centre, Mecca
features: Hotel and conference hall in a wadi below the Sirat hills; the hall hangs from a cable-net roof.
note: No free photo on Commons. Sources confirm a hanging cable-net roof over the auditorium (1,500 or 2,000 seats, sources differ) with aluminium cover, built 1971-74 with Arup, but not the overall massing, the number of masts or how hotel and hall are arranged. Not drawn.

name: Moulmein Rise
features: 28-storey tower whose bay windows hide 'monsoon windows': slots that let the breeze in and keep rain out.
note: No photo on Commons (Singapore allows freedom of panorama, so a new upload would be fine). I drew a version but removed it: sources confirm a slim north-south slab of 28 storeys with bay windows and perforated panels on the south and metal screens on the north, but not how the bay windows are arranged, so the drawing came out as a generic gridded tower.

name: Wasit Wetland Centre
features: Visitor centre sunk into the ground: a ramp leads down to a long glazed gallery looking into the bird aviaries.
note: Commons has about 20 'Wasit Wetland' files (CC BY-SA 4.0); the ones I looked at (Wasit wetland.jpg, Wasit Wetland center.jpg, center 0, 2, 3, Wasit Wetland.jpg) show the lagoon and birds, not the building. File:Wasit Wetland Centre.jpg is an interior. Unchecked: Wasit Wetland center 1 and 4 (portrait). The sunken form is hard to show in elevation, so not drawn.

name: Kamanar Secondary School
features: Classrooms of on-site clay under catenary vaults, shaded by raised metal roofs and timber lattice walls.
note: No photo on Commons. Sources confirm clay catenary vaults covered by metal sheeting on a timber structure, timber lattice infill and classroom modules around tree squares, but not the shape of the metal roof, so not drawn. Year 2021 is from memory; check.

name: Khudi Bari
features: Two-level bamboo frame with steel joints; the upper floor sits six feet up as a refuge from floods.
note: No photo on Commons. Sources describe the frame, joints and two levels but not the roof form or proportions, so not drawn. Built in several places from about 2020; no single completion year found, so year left blank. Bangladesh has no freedom of panorama for buildings by living architects.

name: West Wusutu Village Community Centre
by: Zhang Pengju, Inner Mongolian Grand Architecture Design
features: Village centre built from bricks salvaged from local demolition, for elders, children, artists and Hui Muslims.
note: No photo on Commons. Sources describe purpose, reclaimed bricks and a sunken central area that becomes a pool, but not the massing, so not drawn.

name: Vision Pakistan
features: Vocational school for young people behind colourful pierced-metal jali screens, around a tree-filled atrium.
note: No photo on Commons. Storey count and completion year not found, so not drawn and year left blank.

name: Wonder Cabinet
features: Three-storey concrete hub of workshops, studios and a radio station around a void, above Al-Karkafeh valley.
note: No photo on Commons. Exterior form not described in what I could read, so not drawn.

name: Salinger House
features: Chengal timber house raised on stilts, its plan made of triangles, joined without metal fasteners.
note: No photo on Commons (Wikipedia's lead image Salinger_House.png appears to be a local file). Sources do not describe the roof, so not drawn. Wikipedia says the house was later moved to Paroi, Seremban.

name: Micro Yuan'er Children's Library and Art Centre
features: A 9 m² children's library of plywood and ink-tinted concrete slipped under a hutong roof, beside an old scholar tree.
note: No photo on Commons. The work is inside an existing courtyard house, so an exterior elevation would show the old building, not the intervention. Not drawn.

name: Renovation of Niemeyer Guest House
by: East Architecture Studio (Nicolas Fayad, Charles Kettaneh)
features: Niemeyer's guest house at the Tripoli fair, made a workshop for local carpenters with reversible steel, glass, plywood.
note: Category:Rachid Karami International Fair in Tripoli has about 45 free photos of the fair, but none is labelled as the guest house. Someone who can compare them with published photos may find it. Form not established, so not drawn. Commissioned for Minjara, a Tripoli wood-industry initiative.

name: Alliance Franco-Sénégalaise, Kaolack
features: Cultural centre with library and performance space, mostly open to the air; only a small part is enclosed.
note: No photo on Commons. Sources give load-bearing concrete block and concrete roofs but no description of the form. Not drawn.

name: Nail Çakırhan Residence
features: Timber-framed house with white lime walls, deep eaves, a loggia along its length and a polygonal central hall.
note: No photo on Commons. Built by a poet with two local carpenters; the award was controversial as he had no formal training. Storeys and roof form not confirmed, so not drawn. Akyaka has many free photos of later houses in his style; they are not this house.

name: Courtyard Houses, Agadir
features: 17 single-storey row houses rebuilt after the 1960 earthquake, each with five private patios and a service court.
note: No photo on Commons. The idea lives in the plan (interlocking patios), which an elevation cannot show and which I could not see. Archnet gives 1964, others 1965.

name: Medical Centre, Mopti
features: Low banco-earth clinics and wards around a courtyard, with brise-soleils, deep overhangs and clerestory vents.
note: Possible photo: File:Mopti, la Vénise du Mali, le CSRéf retouché.jpg (1918x1077, CC BY-SA 4.0) shows Mopti's Centre de Santé de Référence, low buildings with perforated claustra screens. It may be Ravéreau's centre, but I could not confirm it, so it is not listed as a photo. Owner could check against Archnet's photos.

name: Concrete at Alserkal Avenue
features: Four warehouses made an arts venue: translucent polycarbonate front, full-height doors, 8 m pivoting walls inside.
note: No photo on Commons (UAE has no freedom of panorama). Front width and height not found; a drawing would be a generic shed, so not drawn.

name: Morocco Pavilion, Expo 2020 Dubai
features: 22 stacked rammed-earth boxes, about 34 m high, around a courtyard and a ramped street inside.
note: No photo on Commons. How the 22 volumes stack is not described, so not drawn. Expo opened October 2021.

name: Muttrah Fish Market
features: Market under a sweeping canopy of 2,400 aluminium slats; perforated concrete walls let sea air through.
note: Commons category exists but its files are Flickr photos from 2010, before Snøhetta's building (2017/2018), so they show the old market. Canopy shape not pinned down, so not drawn.

name: Gaoligong Museum of Handcraft Paper
features: Village museum of small linked pavilions in local timber, bamboo and handmade paper.
note: No photo on Commons. Facts beyond the shortlist (materials, 2010, cluster of small volumes) are from memory and need checking; form not established, so not drawn.

name: Bhong Mosque
by: Rais Ghazi Mohammad (patron) with local craftsmen
features: Village mosque built and decorated over fifty years, 1932-82, crowded with domes, minarets and ornament.
note: Wikipedia names no architect; the patron's name is from memory, check. The award was controversial (praised for craft, criticised as kitsch); worth a line if the owner wants it. Many more free photos on Commons.
